text:
morgan: quick help pls — trying to surface raw log lines for request_id=rt-9f4b2 (trace_id=1a2b3c4d) in staging. trace shows spans but the "Open logs" panel is empty. any console/CLI recipes? @ida :wave:

ida: couple checks — confirm the span actually has a request_id/span attribute. Traces UI: Observability -> Traces -> search 1a2b3c4d -> open span -> inspect Attributes (look for request_id, http.request_id, x-request-id).

ida: if span has no link attr, the console "open related logs" will be blank. fallback is to search logs by time window and id via obsctl or s3. example obsctl: 

```
# 10s-10m window examples, widen if noisy
obsctl logs query --from 2026-03-15T12:01:30Z --to 2026-03-15T12:06:30Z \
  --filter 'request_id:rt-9f4b2 OR http.request_id:rt-9f4b2 OR trace_id:1a2b3c4d' --output jsonl | jq -r '.[].message'
```

ida: if obsctl not available, we keep a read-only S3 mirror for staging logs:
```
# pull the hour folder then grep
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-logs-staging/2026/03/15/12/ ./12-hour --recursive --profile redwood-readonly
grep -n "rt-9f4b2\|1a2b3c4d" -R ./12-hour | head
```

sanju: note — some services only set x-request-id or http.request_id, others put request_id in structured json under fields like `ctx.request.id`. Try broad filters. For json logs, I usually do: 
```
jq -c 'select(.request_id=="rt-9f4b2" or .http.request_id=="rt-9f4b2" or .trace_id=="1a2b3c4d")' logs.jsonl
```

tracebot: indexer: trace 1a2b3c4d indexed at 2026-03-15T12:02:18Z 1 span_links

ida: tracebot shows span_links=0 — means no span->log correlation metadata. Causes: middleware not copying request id to span attrs, or log ingest pipeline dropped the field.

ida: options: 1) quick fix: add request_id attribute to spans in the service (middleware change). 2) hunt by time/service with obsctl/s3. If you know the service name, add `--service my-service` to obsctl to reduce noise.

morgan: got it. how big a time window should I pick? trace start is 2026-03-15T12:02:17Z.

ida: for low-traffic: +-1m. busy endpoints: +-5m or even +-10m. start small, widen if no matches. also add `--limit 1000` to obsctl if you're getting rate-limited.

sanju: one more workflow tip — save a reusable Logs query in Console: Logs -> New Query: `request_id:{{id}} OR trace_id:{{id}}` then set lookback to 15m, save as "reqid-hunt". good for repeated investigations and alerts.

morgan: thanks — ran obsctl with 10m window + x-request-id filter and found the error lines. closing loop. :white_check_mark:
